thread:
emma: quick follow-up from today's AH  wanted to capture a few concrete asks for my team re: the "spend thermostat" changes and the new fastpath for customer-blocking purchases. specific Qs: new approval bands, p-card limits, and how the 'redwood-light' fastpath works for demos/incidents. cc @camille @rahul

camille (CFO): tl;dr: runway comfortable but we need tighter discretionary controls. we're introducing clearer bands, project-level allotments, and a fastpath we call 'redwood-light' for urgent customer-impact buys. details below.

emma: can you list the approval bands so I can update the runbook?

camille (CFO): sure. effective immediately: under $1,500 = manager approval only (no ticket); $1,500$15,000 = procurement + finance required; $15,000$150,000 = senior finance + procurement sign-off; > $150,000 = CFO + legal + procurement and enterprise onboarding. we also have project-level allotments for repeat infra spend (see below).

ryan (eng): what's a project-level allotment? can teams pre-allocate budget for predictable infra usage?

rahul (procurement): yes  teams can request a project allotment (monthly cap with pre-approved vendors). typical approval: procurement + finance review the requested cap and expected SKU list; once approved, purchases from the allotment up to the cap don't require individual approvals. to set one up, submit the Project Allotment form and include historical spend for 3 months. turnaround ~5 business days if packet is complete.

emma: p-card caps? who can request exceptions?

camille (CFO): p-card single-transaction cap = $2,500, rolling monthly cap = $11,000. exceptions allowed for project leads via Spend Request with two approvers listed. p-cards cannot pay for new-vendor onboarding fees above $2,500.

lina (ops): ops contingency note: we maintain a small ops pool for immediate demo/unblock needs up to $5k. to use it, DM ops with a 1-line justification + expected procurement completion ETA.

emma: explain 'redwood-light' fastpath for customer-impact buys?

camille (CFO): 'redwood-light' is the expedite flow for verified customer-impact events (demos, incidents causing revenue impact). process: 1) file Spend Request, tag "redwood-light", include customer impact and cost center; 2) ping @rahul + @lina in the thread; 3) procurement may issue a temp PO or approve a p-card exception up to $10k while onboarding completes. CFO sign-off required for > $15k. target unblock SLA = 24hrs for validated demo blocks, 48hrs for other incidents.

olivia (legal): legal caveat: any purchase that implies data access, cross-border processing, or SLA changes must route to legal regardless of amount. include the contract intake if applicable.

tom (finance-bot): automated guardrail: cardholders approaching 75% of monthly cap get a DM; any attempted swipe above single-txn cap auto-blocks and opens a Spend Request draft to streamline approvals.

emma: any templates or links to post to my team?

camille (CFO): Spend Request: https://internal.redwood.com/spend-request (internal). Project Allotment: https://internal.redwood.com/project-allotment. Email subject template: "Spend Request  [Project]  [Vendor]  Est $XXXX  Redwood-Light: yes/no". rahul and I will drop a short FAQ in #docs by EOD and rahul will host a 20-min office hour tomorrow 10:30am for specific cases.

emma: thank you  will share with my team and book the office hour if we have pending items :thumbsup:
